findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the repo_root cwd-fallback decision belongs in this consolidation ticket or a separate child; if kept here, state explicitly that it is a decision-only (no-code) deliverable so it does not silently expand the spawn refactor's scope.
evidence: Title: 'consolidate the three detached-spawn sites behind one helper'
'Related open question, deliberately NOT changed while fixing 3198: should _config_sources.repo_root's final Path.cwd() fallback DEGRADE rather than raise?'

The repo_root callers are in-process daemon threads (_mcp_writes.py:575, editor.py:523, janitor.py:440, _heartbeat.py:69) which 'cannot be given its own cwd' — a distinct actor/concern from detached children.
AC: 'A recorded decision (accept or change) on repo_root's cwd fallback for long-lived in-process callers.'
findings.finding: The plan bundles two concerns: consolidating the three detached-spawn sites behind one helper (the title's concern) AND a recorded posture decision on `_config_sources.repo_root`'s cwd fallback for long-lived in-process callers (daemon threads at five named sites). The repo_root decision touches a different set of call sites (in-process daemons, not detached children), is framed by the plan itself as a 'Related open question, deliberately NOT changed while fixing 3198,' and is independently decidable/releasable from the spawn-helper consolidation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how `spawn_detached` receives the varying child entry point (e.g. a `module:callable` dotted string plus args) so all three call sites map onto one signature.
evidence: 'It would own the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, the detach flags, the durable cwd, and the never-raise posture; callers would supply only the child entry point and their stderr sink.'
The three sites call back into distinct rebar functions via a `-c` stub
findings.finding: The `spawn_detached(...)` helper must serve three callers that call back into DIFFERENT rebar entry points (push, drain, sweep), but the plan only says callers 'supply the child entry point and their stderr sink' without specifying how the divergent `-c` callback is parameterized, leaving the helper's signature/contract for that varying part unpinned.
findings.location: Scope, first bullet ('callers would supply only the child entry point and their stderr sink')
scenarios: Executor must decide whether 'child entry point' is a module:function string, a code stub, or an argv list — three plausible designs with different call-site rewrites

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that spawn_detached keeps env projection CALLER-supplied (each site passes its already-built child_env, e.g. push.py's project_child_env(...,'unrelated')+REBAR_SYNC_PUSH), so consolidation cannot regress push's credential stripping nor over-apply it to the drain/sweep.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/push.py:204 `child_env = _child_env.project_child_env(os.environ, relationship="unrelated")` then `child_env["REBAR_SYNC_PUSH"] = "always"`
src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:427 `child_env = {**os.environ}` (no credential stripping)
src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:226 `child_env = {**os.environ}` (no credential stripping)

Plan Scope: helper 'would own the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, the detach flags, the durable cwd, and the never-raise posture' — env projection is notably a real per-site divergence not addressed by that list, yet 'Why this matters' names 'an env projection' as a property to fold into the seam
findings.finding: The proposed single spawn_detached helper may over-unify env handling across sites that legitimately differ, creating a golden-hammer risk. push.py projects a credential-stripped env (project_child_env(os.environ, relationship='unrelated')) and injects REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always, whereas enrich_drain and compact_trigger pass a bare {**os.environ}. The plan lists 'an env projection' among properties the helper should own and says callers 'supply only the child entry point and their stderr sink', which reads as the helper owning env policy.
findings.location: Scope bullet 1 ('A single spawn_detached(...) ... callers would supply only the child entry point and their stderr sink') and 'Why this matters' ('an env projection ... will propagate the same way')
scenarios: Consolidation lands and the helper builds env internally as {**os.environ} + PYTHONPATH: push's credential-stripping (JIRA_API_TOKEN/JIRA_PAT removal, RP-04 S3 AC4) silently regresses, leaking adapter secrets to the git-push child.
Alternatively the helper applies push's 'unrelated' projection to the drain/sweep children, changing what env the enrichment/compaction children see.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the Scope so the helper owns only the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, detach flags, durable cwd, stdio discipline, and never-raise posture, and takes the fully-projected child env (and the -c entry stub) as caller-supplied arguments. Explicitly note push.py must continue to pass its project_child_env('unrelated') + REBAR_SYNC_PUSH env unchanged.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the helper accepts a per-caller child env (or an env-projection hook) so push.py's secret-stripping (project_child_env relationship='unrelated') and REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always are preserved, not just the entry point and stderr sink.
evidence: push.py:204 `child_env = _child_env.project_child_env(os.environ, relationship="unrelated")` strips JIRA_API_TOKEN/JIRA_PAT and then sets `child_env["REBAR_SYNC_PUSH"] = "always"`
enrich_drain.py:427 and compact_trigger.py:226 both use `child_env = {**os.environ}` with no secret stripping
Plan lists helper-owned concerns (PYTHONPATH bootstrap, detach flags, durable cwd, never-raise) and caller-supplied concerns (entry point, stderr sink) but never mentions env
findings.finding: The single-helper interface omits per-caller ENV projection, so collapsing push.py onto it risks silently dropping its secret-stripping (project_child_env relationship='unrelated') and its REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always injection.
findings.location: Scope section: 'callers would supply only the child entry point and their stderr sink'
scenarios: The consolidated helper builds env internally from os.environ; the async push child now inherits JIRA_API_TOKEN it previously had stripped (RP-04 S3/AC4 regression)
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'the child env (each caller passes its own projected env; push.py continues to strip adapter secrets and set REBAR_SYNC_PUSH)' to the list of caller-supplied inputs alongside entry point and stderr sink.
